name: 46,XX Difference of Sex Development Induced by Exogenous Maternal-Derived Androgen

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Exogenous Maternal Androgen-Induced 46,XX DSD

criteria.description: Presence of 46,XX karyotype without SRY gene
Documented maternal exposure to exogenous androgens during pregnancy
Clinical evidence of virilization such as clitoromegaly or labioscrotal fusion in the neonate
Imaging or surgical confirmation of normal internal female reproductive structures (uterus, ovaries)
Normal maternal and fetal androgen biosynthesis excluding endogenous causes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of 46,XX karyotype, documented maternal exogenous androgen exposure, and clinical virilization of external genitalia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of endogenous causes of androgen excess such as congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

pathognomonic.notes: Enlargement of the clitoris due to androgen exposure
Partial or complete fusion of the labia resembling scrotum

common.symptomName: Posterior displacement of the vaginal introitus
common.notes: Altered vaginal opening position due to virilization
Presence of uterus and ovaries confirmed by imaging
External genitalia not clearly male or female
Normal levels of estrogens and androgens excluding endogenous excess
searchTerms: normal female hormone levels after birth

occasional.notes: Altered sensory perception in clitoral tissue

occasional.symptomName: Transient maternal virilization symptoms during pregnancy
occasional.notes: Maternal hirsutism or acne due to androgen exposure
searchTerms: temporary male hormone effects in pregnant mother

rare.symptomName: Psychosocial distress related to genital ambiguity
searchTerms: psychosocial issues due to unclear genitalia
mental health impact of ambiguous genitals

rare.notes: Possible side effect of androgen exposure
searchTerms: temporary high blood pressure in pregnancy

laboratory: Normal serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone and androgen levels in neonate
Absence of elevated fetal adrenal androgens
Maternal serum androgen levels elevated during pregnancy
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing normal uterus and ovaries
MRI confirming absence of testicular tissue
genetic: No mutations in CYP21A2 or other congenital adrenal hyperplasia genes
other: History of maternal ingestion or exposure to androgenic drugs or substances during pregnancy

distinguishingFeatures: Female external genitalia with absent or rudimentary internal female organs
Elevated testosterone levels with androgen receptor mutations

redFlags: Severe virilization with ambiguous genitalia at birth
Absence of uterus or ovaries on imaging
Signs of adrenal crisis or salt-wasting
references: Lee PA, Houk CP, Ahmed SF, Hughes IA. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Pediatrics. 2006;118(2):e488-e500.
Hughes IA. Disorders of sex development: a new definition and classification. Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2008;22(1):119-134.
